valid_fixes: Restore ApiHandlerFunction Timeout from 1 to 30 (or any value sufficient for the full DB round-trip)
invalid_patches: Move DB connection outside the handler to module-level to reduce per-invocation latency (masks the fault rather than fixing the timeout)
Reduce connect_timeout in psycopg2 to under 1s to avoid the blocking call (masks the fault)
Increase Lambda memory to speed up execution (insufficient; the bottleneck is network I/O, not CPU)
optimal_diagnostic_path: ace_get_log_tail(ace-bench-stack-api-handler) → shows 'Task timed out after 1.00 seconds' on every invocation
ace_get_lambda_metrics(ace-bench-stack-api-handler, metric=Errors) → elevated error count confirming consistent timeouts
ace_describe_resource(ace-bench-stack, ApiHandlerFunction) → Timeout property is 1; far too short for a DB round-trip
observability_check: functional_test assertion 'order_created' (POST /orders returns 201) fails; Lambda logs show 'Task timed out after 1.00 seconds'
observable_symptom: POST /orders returns 502 on every request. Lambda logs show 'Task timed out after 1.00 seconds'. The function is terminated by the Lambda runtime before the full round-trip (Secrets Manager credential retrieval + database connection + SQL query) can complete. The RDS instance, IAM role, and secret are all healthy.
root_cause: The Lambda function's Timeout is set to 1 second. The per-invocation round-trip — Secrets Manager GetSecretValue, psycopg2 TCP connect, and a SQL INSERT — requires more than 1 second under normal conditions. The Lambda runtime enforces the timeout and kills the handler before it can return a response.
